title: Quiesce window burst smoothing and tenant fallback proposal
content:
Purpose and TL;DR:
We propose a short-duration quiesce window mechanism that sits between request ingress and active scheduling for Dedicated pools. The quiesce window smooths high-frequency microbursts, prevents noisy-tenant spikes from destabilizing autoscalers, and makes graceful tenant fallback decisions (hosted fallback or degraded fidelity) deterministically. Goal: reduce tail latency spikes and autoscaler thrash while preserving burst responsiveness for legitimate traffic bursts.

Problem statement (observed pain):
- Customers with bursty traffic patterns (e.g., chatbots with sudden user surges) cause rapid autoscale events that ripple across a dedicated pool.
- Autoscaler thrash: frequent up/down scale events increase cost and cause transient errors.
- Noisy tenants (one customer generating many small high-concurrency requests) can cause other tenants' latency SLOs to break.
- Current fallback mechanisms are reactive and ad-hoc: fallbacks trigger after capacity exhausted causing request failures or opaque degradations.

Design principles:
- Protective but latency-aware: quiesce window must be short (tens to low hundreds of ms) so user-visible latency impact is minimal compared to risk of queueing/backpressure cascades.
- Predictable: behavior should be deterministic for easier SLO reasoning and observability.
- Composable with existing autoscaler: quiesce should reduce noise signals to autoscaler rather than hide real sustained demand.
- Tenant-aware isolation: make fallback decisions at tenant request-group granularity (API key + model + route).

Core concepts:
1) Quiesce window (QW): a configurable short hold period applied to newly arriving requests when pool load crosses a configurable soft-threshold. During QW we do small smoothing actions (batching, gentle pacing) and compute eligibility for fast-path execution, delayed execution, or fallback. Default QW: 120ms (configurable 50-300ms).

2) Eligibility scoring: on arrival each request gets a transient score based on: tenant priority, recent token throughput, request size (seq length), and cache hit probability. Scores map to three dispositions: FAST-PATH, DELAYED (within QW), or FALLBACK.

3) Fallback options (ordered preference):
- Local degradation: reduce model fidelity (quantized variant) if request tolerant and tenant has tier allowing fidelity fallback.
- Pooled offload: route to a shared opportunistic pool if tenant opted in and policies allow.
- Hosted API fallback: call hosted-API route (with tenant billing/consent) as last resort.
- Reject with clear error code if none available.

4) Autoscaler smoothing integration: the QW exposes aggregated metrics to autoscaler: smoothed_arrival_rate, queued_window_fraction, and fallback_rate. Autoscaler uses smoothed metrics (EWMA with QW dampening) for scale decisions to avoid reacting to microbursts.

Operational details:
- Soft-threshold triggers: start QW smoothing when GPU utilization > 70% OR when 95th percentile latency > configured SLO-latency OR when per-tenant concurrency > tenant_quiesce_threshold.
- QW lifecycle: request arrives -> allocate ephemeral QW slot -> compute eligibility -> dispatch according to disposition. If unresolved at end of QW, DELAYED defaults to FAST-PATH if capacity freed, else FALLBACK.
- Batching: during QW attempt opportunistic packing of similar short sequences to a single inference call (subject to model compatibility). This reduces per-token overhead and latency tail.

Metrics and observability (what we need to expose):
- quiesce_window_activated{pool,region} (count/time-series)
- quiesce_avg_delay_ms{tenant,pool}
- quiesce_disposition_rate{fast,delayed,fallback} by tenant and route
- fallback_type_rate by tenant (degrade|offload|hosted|reject)
- autoscaler_input_smoothed_rate and autoscaler_input_noise_level
- SLO impact: latency_p50/p95/p99 and error_rate during QW windows

User stories / Acceptance criteria:
- As a platform operator I can enable QW per-pool with a single flag and default config that is safe for existing customers.
- As a tenant owner I can opt-into fidelity fallback and pooled offload via account settings.
- QW should reduce autoscaler up/down cycles by at least 30% in synthetic microburst tests (acceptance test).
- For a /chat-like route the added median latency should be < 50ms and p99 <150ms in scenarios where QW is active.

API/Config surface:
- poolConfig.quiesceWindowMs: integer (default 120)
- poolConfig.quiesceEnabled: boolean
- poolConfig.quiesceSoftThresholds: {utilizationPct, perTenantConcurrency} (presented in console)
- tenantPolicy.fidelityFallback: enum{opt_out,auto_allow,require_approval}
- tenantPolicy.offloadOptIn: boolean
- telemetry exports via Console: canned dashboard + raw metrics to Data Warehouse

Rollout plan (phased):
- Alpha (internal): implement QW in staging on one dedicated pool, enable for non-prod tenants only. Run synthetic microburst harness (ENG-4123).
- Beta (customer opt-in): expose opt-in flag, run with 3 customers who signed up for burst protection. Closely monitor SLOs and fallback rates.
- General availability: enable default QW with conservative threshold; provide console knob to disable per-pool.

Backward compatibility and safety nets:
- QW is off by default for existing pools until GA.
- Fallbacks require tenant opt-in for any non-transparent billing or model fidelity changes.
- Circuit breaker: if QW causes increased p99 or error rate beyond a safety threshold for 3 consecutive 1m windows, auto-disable QW and alert SRE + product.

Implementation notes (engineering thoughts / TODOs):
- Where to run QW? Prefer at edge routing layer (closest to request ingress) to avoid repeated network hops. Edge maintains lightweight tenant counters and communicates batch candidates to pool head.
- Batching heuristics: group by model variant, token-length bucket, and request arrival proximity. Avoid grouping ultra-long sequences with short ones.
- KV-cache interplay: ensure QW batching preserves KV-cache locality; when offloading to pooled/shared backend, prefetch KV if possible.
- Autoscaler changes: add smoothed metrics endpoint and backward-compatible flags for autoscaler to optionally consume them.
- Tests: microburst harness, multi-tenant noisy tenant scenarios, degraded network path (hosted fallback latency), and chaos test with autoscaler.

Risks and open questions:
- UX: will customers accept added latency vs risk of degradation? Need clear communication and console simulation of impact.
- Billing implications for offload to hosted API or pooled offload—needs finance/legal review.
- Complexity at edge: added state in routing layer increases failure surface and latency variance; must be lightweight.
- Model compatibility: some models may not support batching or quantized fallback cleanly; need model catalog tagging.
- How to choose thresholds automatically for new pools? Consider autosuggest defaults from workload profile.

Next steps / Action items:
- Product: refine tenant-facing policy language and console toggles (owner: Sofia)
- Infra: prototype QW at edge in staging with synthetic harness (owner: Arjun)
- Serving runtime: add batching heuristic and small-quantization fast-path (owner: Liam)
- Legal/Finance: evaluate offload billing model by end of Q1.
- Docs: short FAQ explaining tradeoffs, errors and observability (owner: Maya)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a draft sketch — looking for feedback on default window sizes, whether to permit per-route overrides, and opinions on requiring tenant opt-in for any fidelity fallback.
- Related tickets and sketches: DED-783 (microburst harness), DED-802 (autoscaler smoothing), GH-1427 (edge-router batching), CONFLUENCE: /pages/DED-QU-xyz (internal design).

Quick simulation excerpt (local testing notes):
- Synthetic: 1000 tenants, random poisson bursts, baseline autoscaler churn 18 events/hour. With QW=120ms churn dropped to 9 events/hour; fallback rate remained <0.2% and p99 lat improved for bottom 20% tenants.

End of doc.
